questions.q: What did Chia-Jung Tsay's study of music experts reveal?
a: They preferred the same recording when told it was natural talent
They preferred the recording by the harder-working musician
They could tell the difference between the two recordings
They judged the musicians by their years of training
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the experts chose the natural musician even though both recordings were identical.

questions.q: What are Duckworth's two equations for achievement?
a: Talent times effort gives skill, then skill times effort gives achievement
Talent plus skill gives effort, then effort plus luck gives success
Skill divided by effort gives talent, then effort divided by skill gives achievement
Talent times skill gives effort, then effort times luck gives achievement
questions.why: Lesson 2 combines the two equations into talent times effort squared equals achievement.

questions.q: Why does Duckworth say effort counts twice?
a: It builds skill and then turns skill into achievement
It improves both talent and reputation
It doubles the hours you can work each day
It matters more in sports than in other fields
questions.why: Lesson 2 says effort is counted once when building skill and again when applying it.

questions.q: What is the problem with only having a big dream?
a: Thinking about it daily can feel depressing without small wins
It makes you too satisfied to keep working
It narrows your options too early
It attracts jealousy from people around you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the big vision needs small daily goals to provide wins and motivation.

questions.q: How does Duckworth suggest staying motivated for the long haul?
a: Pair a large vision with small daily goals
Rely on willpower and avoid all distractions
Track only your long-term results
Change your goal whenever progress stalls
questions.why: Lesson 3 says small daily goals and a big scary dream are both needed.
